key_insight: A slice-wise, clinically structured reasoning dataset can teach a 2D-pretrained multimodal model stronger 3D spatial understanding without full 3D pretraining.
clinical_relevance: This could improve interpretable volumetric reading in medical imaging by helping models track anatomy across slices and reduce spatial reasoning errors.
method: Built a large-scale structured reasoning dataset from 3D scans using slice-wise synthesis.
Modeled radiologist-style workflow: global priors -> per-slice observations -> synthesized Chain-of-Thought.
Instruction-tuned a 2D-pretrained MLLM on the synthesized data to boost volumetric comprehension.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant gains across multiple 3D medical benchmarks, with the tuned model approaching resource-intensive native 3D architectures.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of synthesized reasoning traces, and real-world deployment still needs careful validation across scanners, modalities, and clinical settings.
paper_title: Towards Enhancing 3D Spatial Reasoning in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
